c.tagline: Gateway to sacred Mount Tai, holiest of China's five great peaks.

taxi.fareNote: Metered from about 8 CNY; most locals hail rides through the Didi app, and cash is rarely used - drivers expect Alipay or WeChat Pay.

emergency.note: Police 110, ambulance 120, fire 119. Little English on the line; have your hotel or a translation app assist.

avoid.reason: Watch for pushy touts, unofficial guides and overpriced taxis around the Mount Tai entrances and Dai Temple.

hood_desc: The historic heart around Dai Temple (Daimiao) and the Daizong Fang archway, where pilgrims begin the ascent of Mount Tai; a walkable old-city core of temple walls, the Dai Temple museum, and souvenir lanes - best for first-timers who want the sacred sights on foot.

The modern downtown of Taishan District along Dongyue Street and Hongmen Road, with the main shopping, hotels, and the train-station connections; the most convenient central base for getting around the city.

The larger western urban district of Daiyue, more residential and local with wide new avenues, markets, and everyday eateries; quieter and cheaper than the tourist core, good for a calm, authentic stay.

The Mount Tai trailhead zone around Hongmen (Red Gate) and Tianwai Village at the mountain's southern base, where the climbing path and the cable-car buses start; stay here to be first up the peak for sunrise, amid temples and trail teahouses.
The Gaoxin (High-Tech) Development Zone on the city's outskirts, a planned district of new office parks, malls, and business hotels; modern and orderly but away from the historic sights.
lodging: Holiday Inn Express Taian City Center
Hanting Express Tai'an Tai Mountain Dai Temple

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: City buses generally run from around 6:00 AM to 9:00-10:00 PM; late-night travel relies on Didi or taxis. Tourism Buses 61 and 62 link the train stations to the Mount Tai trailheads.
transit.note: Tai'an has no metro or tram; an extensive city bus network (including Tourism Buses to the Mount Tai gates) plus taxis and Didi cover the city. The two high-speed-rail stations, Tai'an and Taishan, are the main long-distance gateways.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning Alipay or WeChat Pay QR codes on board, or with exact cash (about 1-2 CNY per ride); a transit QR/card is available but mobile pay dominates.

air: No commercial airport in Tai'an; nearest is Jinan Yaoqiang International Airport (TNA, ~75 km), reached via high-speed rail to Jinan plus transfer
bus: Tourism Buses 61/62 to Mount Tai trailheads
Intercity coaches to Jinan, Qufu, and other Shandong cities

car.idp: Required (Chinese licence/permit needed; foreign licences not valid)

train: Tai'an Station (Jinan-Qingdao / Beijing-Shanghai HSR corridor) - high-speed trains to Beijing, Shanghai, Jinan, Qufu, Qingdao, Nanjing
Taishan Station (conventional and some high-speed services, closer to Dai Temple/Mount Tai)

airport.name: Jinan Yaoqiang International Airport (TNA) - nearest, ~75 km north; Tai'an has no commercial airport

transit.m: High-speed rail is the primary gateway: Tai'an/Taishan stations to Jinan West in ~20 min, then transfer for the airport
Jinan Metro Line 3 / airport shuttle bus from Jinan to Yaoqiang Airport (~40-60 min)
Direct Tai'an-Jinan Yaoqiang Airport shuttle coach (~90 min, several daily)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in restaurants, taxis, or hotels; service staff may even refuse it.
